Certainly! Here’s your **12-week integrated muscle gain plan** for your 26-year-old vegan client, including training phases, cardio, nutrition, intensity strategies, and lifestyle guidance. This summary is designed for easy reference and implementation.

---

# **12-Week Vegan Muscle Gain Plan: Integrated Summary**

---

## **Client Profile**
- **Age:** 26
- **Diet:** Strict vegan (no animal, fish, eggs, dairy)
- **Experience:** Recreational lifter
- **Goal:** Muscle gain (hypertrophy)
- **Protein Target:** 150g/day (plant-based only)
- **Gym Access:** Full gym

---

## **Programme Structure**

### **Phases**
1. **Weeks 1–4:** Foundation & Volume
2. **Weeks 5–8:** Progressive Overload
3. **Weeks 9–12:** Intensification & Specialization (High Intensity)

### **Weekly Layout**
- **Day 1:** Upper Body A
- **Day 2:** Lower Body A
- **Day 3:** Rest/Active Recovery + Cardio
- **Day 4:** Upper Body B
- **Day 5:** Lower Body B
- **Day 6:** Rest/Active Recovery + Cardio
- **Day 7:** Rest/Active Recovery + Cardio (optional) + Cheat Meal

---

## **Resistance Training Details**

### **Phase 1: Foundation & Volume (Weeks 1–4)**
- **Reps:** 10–15
- **Sets:** 3–4
- **Rest:** 60–90 sec
- **Focus:** Technique, work capacity, moderate weights

### **Phase 2: Progressive Overload (Weeks 5–8)**
- **Reps:** 8–12
- **Sets:** 3–4
- **Rest:** 60–90 sec
- **Focus:** Increase weights, introduce drop sets on isolation lifts

### **Phase 3: Intensification & Specialization (Weeks 9–12)**
- **Reps:** 4–8 (compounds), 8–15 (isolation)
- **Sets:** 4–5 (compounds), 3–4 (isolation)
- **Rest:** 60–75 sec (compounds), 30–45 sec (isolation)
- **Focus:** Heavy loads, intensity techniques (drop sets, rest-pause, supersets, slow eccentrics)

---

### **Sample Weekly Split**

| Day      | Session                | Cardio                | Notes                |
|----------|------------------------|-----------------------|----------------------|
| Day 1    | Upper Body A           | —                     |                      |
| Day 2    | Lower Body A           | —                     |                      |
| Day 3    | Rest/Active Recovery   | LISS Cardio           | 20–30 min            |
| Day 4    | Upper Body B           | —                     |                      |
| Day 5    | Lower Body B           | —                     |                      |
| Day 6    | Rest/Active Recovery   | MIIT or LISS Cardio   | 20–30 min            |
| Day 7    | Rest/Active Recovery   | Optional LISS Cardio  | **Cheat Meal**       |

---

### **Upper Body A (Sample)**
- Barbell Bench Press
- Seated Cable Row
- Dumbbell Shoulder Press
- Lat Pulldown
- Dumbbell Biceps Curl
- Triceps Rope Pushdown

### **Lower Body A (Sample)**
- Barbell Back Squat
- Romanian Deadlift
- Leg Press
- Seated Leg Curl
- Standing Calf Raise

### **Upper Body B (Sample)**
- Incline Dumbbell Press
- Pull-Up or Lat Pulldown
- Machine Shoulder Press
- Chest Supported Row
- Cable Lateral Raise
- EZ Bar Curl

### **Lower Body B (Sample)**
- Deadlift
- Bulgarian Split Squat
- Leg Extension
- Lying Leg Curl
- Seated Calf Raise

**Progression:**  
- Add weight or reps each week if all sets/reps are completed with good form.
- In Phase 3, use intensity techniques as described above.

---

## **Cardio Integration**

- **Weeks 1–4:** 2x/week LISS (20–25 min, brisk walk, bike, elliptical)
- **Weeks 5–8:** 2–3x/week (add MIIT: 1 min moderate, 1 min brisk, repeat for 20 min)
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3x/week (2x LISS, 1x MIIT, 20–30 min/session)
- **Timing:** On rest/active recovery days or after lifting (never before)

---

## **Nutrition Guidelines**

- **Calories:** TDEE + 250–350 kcal surplus
- **Protein:** 150g/day (plant-based)
- **Carbs/Fats:** Fill remainder of calories with complex carbs and healthy fats

### **High-Protein Vegan Foods**
- Tofu, tempeh, seitan
- Lentils, chickpeas, black beans
- Edamame, soy milk
- Quinoa, buckwheat, oats
- Vegan protein powder (pea/rice blends)
- Nuts/seeds (supplemental)

### **Sample High-Protein Breakfasts**
- Tofu scramble with beans and toast (~30g protein)
- Protein oats with vegan protein powder (~25g protein)
- Tempeh breakfast sandwich (~22g protein)
- Vegan yogurt parfait with protein powder (~30g protein)

### **Post-Workout Meal Ideas**
- Tofu & quinoa bowl
- Lentil & brown rice stir-fry
- Vegan protein shake with banana
- Tempeh wrap or sandwich

### **Protein Powder Recommendations**
- **Vivo Life Perform** (pea + hemp)
- **Garden of Life Sport** (multi-source)
- **Nuzest Clean Lean Protein** (pea)
- **Orgain Organic Protein** (pea + rice + chia)
- **MyProtein Vegan Blend** (pea + fava bean)
- **Sunwarrior Warrior Blend** (pea + hemp + goji)

---

## **Cheat Meal Guidance**

- **Frequency:** 1x/week (e.g., Sunday)
- **What:** Any vegan meal she enjoys (pizza, burger, dessert, etc.)
- **How:** Eat to satisfaction, not discomfort; resume normal eating at next meal

---

## **Supplements**

- **Creatine Monohydrate:** 5g/day (vegan-friendly)
- **Vitamin B12:** 1000mcg/week or as per guidelines
- **Vitamin D3:** 2000 IU/day (vegan source)
- **Omega-3 (Algal Oil):** 250–500mg DHA/EPA/day
- **Iron:** Monitor status, supplement if needed

---

## **Recovery & Lifestyle**

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours/night
- **Hydration:** 2–3L water/day
- **Mobility:** 10–15 min dynamic warm-up before sessions, static stretching post-workout
- **Active Recovery:** Light cardio, yoga, or walking on rest days

---

## **Progress Tracking**

- **Photos & Measurements:** Every 4 weeks
- **Strength Log:** Track weights, sets, reps
- **Nutrition Log:** Track protein and calories daily

---

## **Intensity Techniques for Phase 3**

- **Drop Sets:** After last set, reduce weight by 15–25%, rep to failure
- **Rest-Pause Sets:** After last set, rest 10–20 sec, rep to failure, repeat once
- **Supersets:** Pair two exercises back-to-back, rest after both
- **Slow Eccentrics:** Lower weight over 3–4 seconds for increased time under tension

---

**This plan is designed to maximize muscle gain, support vegan nutrition, and keep training engaging and effective. Adjust volume or intensity as needed based on recovery and progress.**

---

**Let me know if you want a printable PDF, exercise substitutions, or more meal ideas!**

## **Cardio Integration Principles**

- **Frequency:** 2–3 sessions per week
- **Type:** Low-to-moderate intensity steady-state (LISS) and/or moderate-intensity interval training (MIIT)
- **Duration:** 20–30 minutes per session
- **Timing:** Preferably on rest days or after resistance training (never before lifting)
- **Goal:** Support cardiovascular health, aid recovery, and manage body composition without excessive calorie burn

---

## **12-Week Cardio Structure**

### **Weeks 1–4: Foundation**

- **2x/week LISS** (e.g., brisk treadmill walk, incline walk, cycling, elliptical)
- **20–25 minutes/session**
- **Intensity:** 60–70% max heart rate (can hold a conversation)

**Example Schedule:**
- **Day 3:** LISS Cardio (rest/active recovery day)
- **Day 6 or 7:** LISS Cardio (rest/active recovery day)

---

### **Weeks 5–8: Progressive Overload**

- **2–3x/week** (add a third session if recovery is good)
- **1–2x/week LISS:** 25–30 minutes/session
- **1x/week MIIT:** 20 minutes/session (e.g., 1 min moderate pace, 1 min brisk pace, repeat)

**Example Schedule:**
- **Day 3:** LISS Cardio
- **Day 6:** MIIT Cardio (or LISS if preferred)
- **Optional Day 7:** LISS Cardio (if energy and recovery allow)

---

### **Weeks 9–12: Intensification**

- **3x/week** (as tolerated)
- **2x/week LISS:** 25–30 minutes/session
- **1x/week MIIT:** 20–25 minutes/session

**Example Schedule:**
- **Day 3:** LISS Cardio
- **Day 6:** MIIT Cardio
- **Day 7:** LISS Cardio

---

## **Sample Cardio Workouts**

### **LISS (Low-Intensity Steady-State)**
- Treadmill walk at 3.5–4.0 mph, 3–5% incline
- Stationary bike at moderate pace
- Elliptical at steady, moderate resistance

### **MIIT (Moderate-Intensity Interval Training)**
- 1 min moderate pace (jog or fast walk), 1 min brisk pace (run or power walk), repeat for 20 minutes
- Rowing machine: 1 min steady, 1 min push, repeat

---

## **Cardio & Nutrition Notes**

- **Fuel:** Ensure she eats a small carb/protein snack 30–60 min before cardio if fasted cardio leaves her low on energy.
- **Hydration:** Emphasize water intake, especially on cardio days.
- **Recovery:** Stretch after cardio, especially lower body.

   - Aim for **20–25g protein per serving**.

3. **Low Sugar & Additives:**  
   - Minimal added sugars, artificial sweeteners, or fillers.

4. **Third-Party Tested:**  
   - Look for brands that test for purity and heavy metals.

5. **Allergen-Free:**  
   - Ensure it’s free from dairy, eggs, and other animal products (most vegan powders are, but always check).

---

## **Cheat Meal Day Guidelines**

### **Frequency**
- **Once per week** (e.g., Saturday or Sunday—whichever fits her lifestyle best)

### **What is a Cheat Meal?**
- A single meal (not an entire day) where she can enjoy foods outside her usual plan, without tracking calories or macros.
- Still vegan—no animal products, eggs, dairy, or fish.

### **How to Approach It**
- **Enjoyment:** Choose favorite vegan foods—pizza, burgers, desserts, etc.
- **Portion:** Eat to satisfaction, not to discomfort.
- **No Guilt:** This is part of the plan and can help with long-term consistency.
- **Hydration:** Drink plenty of water before and after.
- **Resume normal eating** at the next meal.

---

## **Sample Vegan Cheat Meal Ideas**

- **Vegan Pizza:** With vegan cheese, veggies, plant-based sausage or pepperoni
- **Vegan Burger & Fries:** Plant-based patty, whole grain bun, toppings, sweet potato or regular fries
- **Vegan Sushi:** Avocado rolls, tofu rolls, tempura veggies
- **Vegan Mac & Cheese:** Cashew or coconut-based sauce, pasta, breadcrumbs
- **Vegan Dessert:** Brownies, cookies, ice cream (coconut, almond, or oat-based)
- **Vegan Takeout:** Thai, Indian, or Chinese food (tofu curry, vegan pad thai, veggie fried rice, etc.)

---

## **Tips for Success**

- **Plan ahead:** Pick the meal in advance to look forward to it and avoid overindulgence.
- **Stay vegan:** Double-check restaurant or packaged food ingredients.
- **Enjoy mindfully:** Savor the meal, eat slowly, and stop when satisfied.
- **Don’t skip protein:** If possible, include a protein source (tofu, tempeh, seitan, beans, vegan meat) in the cheat meal.
- **Hydrate:** Cheat meals can be higher in sodium—drink extra water.

---

## **How It Fits the Programme**

- **Psychological boost:** Satisfies cravings, reduces feelings of restriction.
- **Metabolic benefit:** Occasional higher-calorie meals can support metabolism during a muscle gain phase.
- **Social flexibility:** Allows for meals out with friends or family.

### **Intensity Technique Explanations**
- **Drop Set:** After last set, immediately reduce weight by 15–25% and continue to failure.
- **Rest-Pause:** After last set, rest 10–20 seconds, then perform as many reps as possible; repeat once.
- **Superset:** Perform two exercises back-to-back, then rest.
- **Slow Eccentric:** Lower the weight over 3–4 seconds to increase time under tension.

---

### **Progression & Recovery**
- **Aim to increase weight or reps each week** on main lifts.
- **Monitor fatigue:** If recovery suffers, reduce intensity techniques to 1–2 per session.
- **Prioritize sleep, hydration, and nutrition** to support recovery.

---

### **Cardio**
- Keep as previously structured (2–3x/week, LISS or MIIT, not HIIT to avoid excessive fatigue).

---

### **Nutrition**
- Maintain calorie surplus and 150g+ protein/day.
- Consider a post-workout meal with 30–35g protein and 50–70g carbs for optimal recovery.
